result.summary: Idiom/scope/decision-record gate PASS. This diff (git diff main...HEAD) touches no gen_statem/supervision code at all -- test/fixture-only, no lib/letflow/engine/expr.ex change (confirmed via git diff --stat, matching SECURITY-REVIEWER's independent confirmation) -- so REVIEWER charter questions 1-2 (state-machine idiom, supervision integrity) do not apply to this diff. Test idiom: expr_differential_corpus_test.exs is a plain `ExUnit.Case, async: true` calling the single composed production entry point Expr.evaluate_condition/2 (not a hand-assembled translate/parse/eval chain), matching expr_test.exs's own async/no-Repo precedent. Property-style convention: process_instance_test.exs, cited by both the design doc and WF-02_requirement_implementation.md as precedent, no longer exists in the tree (retired per REQ-046 process_instance retirement) -- the design doc (Sec 6) anticipated this and explicitly resolved 'property-style' to mean one test with an internal loop over a fixed data table, correctly distinguished from this codebase's actual StreamData convention (test/letflow/oidc/claim_mapping_property_test.exs, genuinely generative, appropriate for its unbounded input space but not for this fixed 15-entry corpus). Implementation matches that resolution: one test block, one Enum.reduce/3 loop, per-entry condition_id in failure messages. EXPECTED_UNSUPPORTED scaffolding: justified forward-compatibility, not speculative complexity -- design doc Sec 4/6/8-OQ1 explicitly requires the branch to exist despite zero entries in conditions_v1.json exercising it, reasoning the corpus is versioned and a future conditions_v2.json could introduce an unsupported construct. Implemented as a real, reachable @expected_unsupported_ids MapSet.new([]) keyed by condition_id (both branches genuinely execute, avoiding a compile-time 'clause will never match' warning under --warnings-as-errors), and correctly avoids re-deriving Expr's private unsupported_cel_feature?/1 detection logic inside test code. Scope creep: none -- no new abstractions/behaviours/macros, fixture is a verbatim byte-for-byte port per design Sec 5, test's assertion counts (evaluated_count==15, expected_unsupported_count==0, sum==15) map directly to acceptance criteria. Decision-record consistency: no conflict -- nothing in this diff touches a framework/library choice; confined to test/ and a design doc. No BLOCKER/MAJOR/MINOR issues found. Step 3 note for ORCH: this requirement's Step 2a (ELIXIR-DEV) already wrote the full test per an approved design, and the test already provides complete coverage of all 15 corpus entries with per-entry assertions and an accounted-for-all-15 count check -- TEST-DESIGNER's role here is confirming coverage completeness (and TEST-DESIGN-VALIDATOR gating that confirmation), not authoring new test code from scratch. Recommend routing TEST-DESIGNER with an explicit note that Step 3 is a verification/confirmation pass over 02a's existing test, not new authorship.
